No, that is not correct. A flat plateau on a capillary-pressure curve indicates that the rock has a **very narrow pore-size distribution**. 

In a capillary pressure curve, the **slope** of the curve is related to the **pore-size distribution**. A **flat plateau** suggests that the rock has **uniform pore sizes** (i.e., narrow distribution), while a **steep curve** indicates a **broad pore-size distribution**. 

If you observe a flat region, it means that the capillary pressure remains relatively constant over a range of saturation levels, which is characteristic of a rock with **uniform pore sizes**. 

So, the statement that a flat plateau means a broad pore-size distribution is **incorrect**.
